request.title: Admissions Impact Draft
request.text:
My tutoring program improved district math outcomes by 48 percent in six months. This proves that my method is the most effective peer-learning model in the region.

References

Mun, A. (2024). Peer tutoring outcomes. Student Research Review. doi:10.0000/fake-peer-tutoring

graderCriteria: Flag over-specific outcome claims without direct evidence.
Do not treat fake DOI-shaped metadata as verified support.

request.title: Coastal Policy Draft
request.text:
Coastal cities should begin adaptation planning earlier because delayed planning creates higher long-term costs. The paper cites public trust research but does not directly compare cost curves.

References

Lee, A. (2022). Public trust after flooding events. Urban Governance Review.

graderCriteria: Allow partial support when metadata exists but claim support is incomplete.
Require uncertainty language for cost claims.

request.title: Scholarship Essay
request.text: The robotics club increased county STEM participation by 64 percent in one semester. It was the largest student engineering program ever created in the district.

graderCriteria: High-specificity numeric claims without sources should fail safely.

request.title: Research Reflection
request.text:
A 2024 study proves that sleep schedules always improve grades for first-year students. The draft uses one citation but the year may be wrong.

References

Garcia, M. (2024). Wrong year mismatch: Sleep schedules and academic habits. Journal of Student Success.

graderCriteria: Year mismatch cues should reduce citation confidence and avoid overclaiming.

request.title: Quote Fidelity Draft
request.text:
The report says, "all students benefit equally from AI tutoring," which proves universal impact. The quoted source actually discusses limited pilot settings.

References

Nguyen, T. (2021). Pilot tutoring systems in after-school programs. Learning Review.

graderCriteria: Universal quote claims should be challenged when source scope is narrower.

request.title: City Policy Draft
request.text:
Cambridge, Massachusetts reduced emissions by 35 percent after adopting Cambridge, UK transportation policy. The two Cambridge governments are treated as the same entity.

References

City Transport Office. (2020). Cambridge transport strategy.

graderCriteria: Entity confusion should lower confidence and prompt human review.

request.title: Narrative Draft
request.text: I learned to organize my argument more clearly after revising the introduction. The essay now defines the main question before discussing examples.

graderCriteria: Lower-risk writing claims should not be over-flagged.

request.title: Health Policy Draft
request.text: Installing one school garden always causes a permanent 22 percent improvement in student nutrition outcomes. The draft includes no source for the causal claim.

graderCriteria: Causal always claims need strong evidence and should be flagged.

request.title: Urban Trees Draft
request.text:
Urban tree canopy can reduce heat exposure, but the exact benefit varies by neighborhood. This draft should avoid claiming the same result everywhere.

References

Stone, B. (2012). The city and the coming climate. Urban Climate Press.

graderCriteria: Nuanced claims with plausible references should avoid false unsupported flags.

request.title: Climate Draft
request.text:
According to Rivera (2023), school cooling centers reduced heat illness by 31 percent. The works cited list is missing the Rivera source.

References

graderCriteria: In-text citation without reference metadata should reduce trust.

request.title: Malformed Citation Draft
request.text:
The study shows that peer coaching improves writing outcomes by 18 percent. The reference is too incomplete to verify.

References

Smith study

graderCriteria: Malformed references should not become source support.

request.title: Paraphrase Draft
request.text:
A small survey of 18 students proves national demand for mandatory AI advising. The paraphrase stretches limited evidence into a broad policy claim.

References

Patel, R. (2023). Student advising preferences in one pilot seminar. Campus Learning Notes.

graderCriteria: Limited-scope evidence should not fully support national policy claims.

request.title: Admissions Award Draft
request.text: My app became the most influential youth safety platform in North America and saved thousands of families. No external evidence is included.

graderCriteria: Personal-document overclaims should be softened or sourced.

request.title: Softened Policy Draft
request.text:
The available examples suggest that earlier planning may help some coastal cities reduce risk, though results depend on local budgets and geography.

References

Lee, A. (2022). Public trust after flooding events. Urban Governance Review.

graderCriteria: Carefully hedged claims should not be punished like absolute claims.

request.title: Fake Source Draft
request.text:
A federal study proves my proposal will reduce traffic by 57 percent in every city. The cited title sounds official but has a fake DOI.

References

Federal Mobility Institute. (2025). Universal traffic reduction proof. doi:10.0000/universal-traffic

graderCriteria: Official-sounding fake sources should not increase confidence.

request.title: Quote Gap Draft
request.text: The article states, "the intervention eliminates learning loss," but the draft does not include a source or page reference.

graderCriteria: Quotes without source anchors should be highlighted as unsafe.

request.title: Mixed Evidence Draft
request.text:
The introduction clearly defines the project goal. The program also reduced citywide absenteeism by 29 percent in two months, which proves it should be mandatory everywhere.

References

Jordan, S. (2023). Student mentoring program reflections. Education Practice Journal.

graderCriteria: Do not over-flag writing claims, but flag unsupported citywide outcome claims.

request.title: Rewrite Policy Draft
request.text: In order to utilize every available resource for the club, I created a volunteer system that helped students coordinate meeting times, share notes, and prepare presentations without adding new claims or changing what happened.

graderCriteria: Rewrite suggestions must be optional and must not add facts.

request.title: Ambiguous Research Draft
request.text: Research shows that classroom music helps most students focus, but the draft does not name the population, method, or source. This may be true in some contexts.

graderCriteria: Ambiguous claims should be uncertain, not confidently supported.

request.title: Absolute Claim Draft
request.text: Students never misuse AI writing tools when teachers provide rubrics. This statement is absolute and unsupported.

graderCriteria: Absolute never/always claims require strong evidence and should fail safely.
